page.title: Best Power Station Under $200: What the 600 W Label Really Delivers
page.desc: The best power station under $200 on Nov 27, 2026: what its 600 W mode really outputs (300 W), the 5 W the unit draws itself, and hours at 10 to 300 W.
page.answer: Short answer. The best portable power station under $200 is the BLUETTI Elite 30 mini at its Black Friday price: 288 Wh, 300 W AC, 7.3 lb. Its "600 W" mode still outputs 300 W and the unit draws about 5 W itself, so a 10 W router runs about 16 hours by BLUETTI's formula, not 29.

page.after:
$200 is the line because it buys the 300 Wh, 300 W class and nothing larger. Outdoor Gear Lab's tests mark a fridge, kettle, heater and induction burner as unsupported on its 300 W units and estimate about 4 hours for a 60 W CPAP on a 290 Wh station. Every row above has an AC outlet and cost $200 or less on Nov 27, 2026 at the seller named in its price cell. Dealectric does not test units; every figure here is a maker's or a named reviewer's.

The Elite 30 mini is under $200 only at BLUETTI's Black Friday price. Its list price is $249.99.

What the differences mean

Inside the line we rank on watt-hours per dollar paid and on weight.

  • Watt-hours per dollar. Elite 30 mini: 288 Wh ÷ {after:bluetti-elite-30-mini} = 1.52 through our link (1.45 at the store price of {price:bluetti-elite-30-mini}). VTOMAN Jump 600X: 299 ÷ 199.00 = 1.50. EcoFlow RIVER 2 (240): 240 ÷ 189.00 = 1.27. Elite 10 Mini: 128 ÷ 129.99 = 0.98.
  • Weight. BLUETTI gives the Elite 30 mini as 7.3 lb: 288 ÷ 7.3 = 39.5 Wh per lb. NikKTech lists the Jump 600X at 6.64 kg, which is 14.6 lb (6.64 × 2.2046): 299 ÷ 14.6 = 20.5 Wh per lb. EcoFlow gives the RIVER 2 (240) as 7.7 lb: 240 ÷ 7.7 = 31.2 Wh per lb.
  • Energy that reaches the outlet. BLUETTI's manual formula for the Elite 30 mini: 288 Wh × 95% depth of discharge × 90% inverter efficiency = 246 Wh. That is the maker's formula, and we have no named reviewer's measurement for this unit.
  • Time above 300 W. The Jump 600X is the only row that runs a 300 to 600 W load. At 600 W, 299 Wh ÷ 600 W = 0.5 hour at most, before conversion losses.

Left out: the EcoFlow RIVER 3 (245 Wh), because we could read no price for it on Nov 27 at EcoFlow's US store or on Amazon. The EcoFlow RIVER 2 with 256 Wh was $209.00 on Amazon. The Tenergy T320 is {price:tenergy-t320-300wh-power-station} and the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 is {price:bluetti-elite-30-v2}. Solar is also outside the budget: the Elite 30 mini's box holds an AC cable and a car cable but no panel or solar cable. Its manual accepts third-party panels with a 12–28 V open-circuit voltage and MC4 connectors.

What "600 W" means on a 300 W power station

BLUETTI's page for the Elite 30 mini carries a 600 W figure. The manual (p. 16) says of Power Lifting mode: "While the Elite 30 mini can handle such loads, its actual output power is still 300 W." It limits the mode to pure resistive loads rated 300–600 W and names kettles, electric blankets and hair dryers. The mode is off by default and is switched on in the BLUETTI app. A 600 W heating element fed 300 W gives half its rated heat, so the same job takes about twice as long (600 ÷ 300 = 2). For motors and compressors the manual says to keep total power below 300 W, because they can draw 2–4 times their rating at startup.

EcoFlow labels the same class the same way. Its store lists the RIVER 2 (240) as 300 W with 600 W X-Boost, and StorageReview's table for the RIVER 3 reads "300W total (Surge 600W, X-Boost 600W)". Compare these units on 300 W.

The figure that matters more for small loads is what the station uses itself. BLUETTI's manual (p. 24) gives the formula: operation time = capacity × DoD × η ÷ (load + self-consumption), with DoD 95%, η over 90% and self-consumption about 5 W. At η = 90%:

LoadCapacity ÷ loadBLUETTI's formula
10 W (router)28.8 h246 ÷ 15 = 16.4 h
20 W14.4 h246 ÷ 25 = 9.8 h
50 W5.8 h246 ÷ 55 = 4.5 h
60 W (CPAP, Outdoor Gear Lab's example)4.8 h246 ÷ 65 = 3.8 h
100 W2.9 h246 ÷ 105 = 2.3 h
300 W58 min246 ÷ 305 = 48 min

These are estimates from the maker's formula, not measurements. The 85.5% the formula implies (95% × 90%) matches the one measurement we have for this class: StorageReview ran an EcoFlow RIVER 3 into a 300 W fan and got 210 Wh of its rated 245 Wh, which is 85.7%. It took 270 Wh from the wall to refill.

Two settings change the result.

  • ECO mode. It is off by default. Switched on, it cuts the AC output after 1–4 hours below a threshold you set between 10 and 40 W (5–20 W for DC). The manual says to disable it "when connecting small devices or critical appliances such as lights and refrigerators". Leave it off for a router or a phone charger.
  • Cold. The manual gives a charging range of 32–104 °F and a discharging range of −4 to 104 °F. Below freezing the unit runs loads but does not take a charge.

Not recommended

AFERIY P040. AFERIY's store listed it at $169.00 on Nov 27 and flagged it unavailable. The listing title says 288 Wh while its description says 256 Wh. We would not buy on a capacity figure the maker's own page states two ways.

Any 300 W station for a kettle or space heater. None of the 300 W rows runs one at full power, whatever the 600 W label says. For a load between 300 and 600 W, the VTOMAN Jump 600X is the one row with the continuous rating for it.
